dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you?
Yes, good morning. Is it all right if I ask about the drain on our corner? It's the same drain. Again.
Sure, go ahead. What's the address?
Thirty-one Howard Street. Fifth Ward. Okafor. My wife Priya called you in January, and my son called after the big storm in February. So you probably know us by now. Unfortunately.
Okafor, Howard Street. Yeah, I do remember. Hang on, let me pull it up. [pause] Sorry, is that music on your end? I'm getting a little bit of an echo.
Oh, my speaker. The little one on the counter. Is it all right if I just... one second. [pause] Better?
Much better, thanks. Okay, I've got the file. What happened this time?

The rain, Friday into Saturday. The drain backed up again. Whole street in front of the house, a big pond, right up to our top step. Saturday morning I'm standing at the door looking at a lake. On Howard Street.
Did any water get into the house?
No. The basement stayed dry this time. Thank God. But that's luck, that's not because anything got fixed. It stopped raining before it got high enough, that's all.
Okay. Good that it stayed dry, at least.

Yes, good. Is it all right if I say something, though? It's been in the basement twice already this winter. January, after that coastal storm, and then the nor'easter at the end of February, that one was eight inches. The rec room carpet, we pulled it all out. And both times it's the same thing. The water comes up out of the street drain first. You can watch it. It bubbles up out of the grate, fills the street, and then it comes into the house. So when I see the street fill up Saturday, I know what's next.
Right. I've got both of those in here. January tenth, and the twenty-second of February.

So. In January somebody came and cleaned the leaves off the grate. Off the top. Very nice. Then February they came with the truck, the jetting, and they said it was partly blocked down there. Then a supervisor called my son and said a bigger fix is being looked at. Looked at. No date. And now here we are, the street's a pond again a week and a half later.
I hear you. I'm seeing the jetting on the twenty-fifth and the supervisor callback on the twenty-sixth, and you're right, there's no date on the larger repair yet.

And also, may I ask, did someone already call yesterday? Ivan, the young man who rents our second-floor apartment. He said he was going to call. I told him I'd call too, because, honestly, I don't know if one call does anything.
Yep, there's a note from yesterday morning, same thing, street ponded, basement dry. It went into the repeat-backup file.
The repeat-backup file. Okay. It's a nice thick file, I bet.

[pause] It's getting there, yeah. Look, I'm adding your report to it now, with the depth to the top step, and I'm flagging it to the supervisor again today so he sees there were two calls on this one storm from the same house.

Is it all right if I ask for a number? A work order, a reference, something. Because every time we call, it's a different person in my family and I want to be able to say, this is the number, this is the history, please look.
Absolutely. The whole history's under one file for your address, so that number covers January forward. Got a pen?
Yes. Go ahead.
It's P-W, dash, two six, dash, zero four one eight. Today's note is added under that.
P-W, two six, zero four one eight. Okay. I'll put it on the refrigerator. Next to the last three times.
That works. Anyone in the house can call in with that and whoever picks up sees everything.
And a crew? Will someone come out this time, or no?

There's no new crew date on it right now. The line was just jetted, so this is really in the supervisor's hands for the bigger fix. I'm putting in the note that you're asking for an update on where that stands. Is the number on file still good for a callback, the one ending one-four-zero?
Yes, that's ours. My wife and me, same phone.
Okay, good. If it starts filling up during the next rain, call right then, while it's happening. That gets logged with a time on it and that helps make the case.
While it's happening. Okay. I'll be standing at the door with the phone, then. Like Saturday.
I know it's not what you want to hear. I'll make sure it gets to him today.
All right. Thank you, Denise. Is it all right if I turn my music back on now?
Go right ahead. Take care, Mr. Okafor.
